title: Carry a wafer carrier into a rinse tank by its top bar
instruction: Put the wafer carrier into the rinse tank using its handle, then take the handle off the carrier and stand it on the bench deck.
context: Why: every chip passes through dozens of wet cleans. In university and R&D cleanrooms that prototype new chips, AI hardware included, an operator moves a whole carrier of wafers from bath to bath with a detachable handle (a university cleanroom's RCA-clean SOP: "Using the top captured handle, place the wafer carrier into SC1"). The squeeze handle's feet hook into a notch in each end wall of the carrier; squeezing the curved bow under its top bar spreads them, which is how it goes on and comes off (the maker also sells one with a lock bar). So the carrier hangs safely only while the hand holds the bar alone. The hard part is physical: close on the 14 mm bar without pressing the bow 33 mm below it, carry the 0.75 kg open-top load hanging from it within 15 deg of level, seat it on rests inside a 200 mm tank, then squeeze the bow to free the handle without moving the seated carrier. Done by: wet-bench operators in fabs and users of university cleanrooms, at every bath change.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Wet bench (polypropylene plastic, bolted down; 40 kg in the simulator): a deck 17.5 cm high and 24 cm wide (y -22 to 2) from x 10.0 to 32.2 cm, in front of a recessed quick-dump-rinse tank (drained for this trial: on a real bench it may hold DI water; the simulator has none) with 8 mm walls, inside 200 x 200 mm centred at x 43.0 cm, y -10.0 cm, its floor 8 mm thick on the table and its rim 10 mm proud of the deck. On the tank floor two PFA carrier rests 25 mm high, 21 mm wide and 140 mm long along y, centred 65.5 mm either side of the tank's centre in x, under the carrier's bottom rails. Wafer carrier: Entegris A182-50M (182 series, natural PFA plastic, 143 x 152 x 146 mm: 143 along y, 152 along x; about 0.30 kg) holding 25 test-grade 125 mm silicon wafers 0.625 mm thick (17.9 g each) in its 25 slots at 4.76 mm pitch, upright on the deck centred at x 24.0 cm, y -10.0 cm, stack axis along y, H-bar end toward -y. Each end wall has a notch 60 mm wide, 8 mm high and 6 mm deep in its outer face, 118 mm up. Squeeze handle: Entegris A72-50-03 (natural PFA plastic, 163 x 140 x 183 mm, about 0.15 kg), on the carrier with both feet's tines in the end-wall notches. It is an inverted U: a top bar 14 x 14 mm along y, two legs ending in feet 140 mm wide with a 50 mm tine pointing in, and a curved bow under the bar, 33 mm below it at the middle. The legs are sprung closed at 2000 N/m; squeezing the bow up toward the bar (sprung at 2000 N/m, 20 N at its stop, up 10 mm) spreads them 1.2 mm per mm, up to 12 mm, so the tines come out of the 6 mm notches once the bow is up 5 mm. For real trials the wafers may be 125 mm x 0.5 mm aluminium discs (16.6 g each, shatter-free) in the same slots, and the bench, tank and rests may be built from 8 mm polypropylene sheet and bar to these dimensions, with the tank wall facing the side camera (the -y wall, along x) in clear 8 mm polycarbonate so the rests and tines can be seen. Both arms start in their ready pose. Starting layout fixed; the screenshot shows it.
scoring: The tines may come out of the notches only while the carrier sits on both rests (as below): that is how the handle is taken off for 1.0. Latched zero, at any time even if put right after: once the carrier has been lifted, a tine leaving its notch while the carrier is not sitting on both rests (at any height; judged at the moment it leaves); the carrier falls (within 0.25 s its centre goes down 20 mm further than either hand went: let go or sliding off the fingers; lowering with the hand at any speed is not), tips more than 15 deg from upright (wafers walk out), a gripper touches the carrier (it moves only by its handle; within 3 mm of the carrier in the simulator), or the bench moves more than 5 mm. 0.25: the carrier lifted with every bottom corner at least 20 mm above the deck while both tines are in their notches. 0.5: and then carried over the tank: its centre within 20 mm of the tank's centre in x and y. 0.75: at the end the carrier sits on both rests: its bottom rails within 3 mm above the rests' tops at all four corners, its centre within 30 mm of the tank's centre, upright within 5 deg. 1.0: in addition the handle is off the carrier (at least 10 mm from it everywhere) and standing on its feet on the bench deck (feet within 3 mm of the deck, within 10 deg of upright), no gripper within 30 mm of the carrier or the handle, and neither moving more than 2 mm over the last 2 s. Rungs count in order. 0: anything else, including the untouched start or a carrier never lifted on its handle. Real-trial checks: a fixed side camera level with the rests' tops, looking through the tank's clear -y wall (see setup), plus the wrist video. A tine out is its end visible outside its notch; on the rests is the gap under each rail below a tick drawn 3 mm above each rest's top, at that frame (far corners: steel rule after the trial). The fall is read frame by frame against a tape on the clear wall: the carrier's and the hand's descent over 0.25 s (8 frames at 30 fps); tilt from a phone level on the carrier's end wall and the side video; gripper contact from both videos; the 20 mm lift against the tape; over the tank with tape marks at the middle of the carrier's end walls within 20 mm of tape lines on the rim; seated with a steel rule at the four corners (3 mm) and the phone level (5 deg); the handle off and its feet with a steel rule (10 mm, 3 mm) and the phone level (10 deg); the bench against floor tape (5 mm); stillness from the side video's last 2 s.
reset_notes: Take the handle off, set the carrier back on its taped spot on the deck, check all 25 wafers (or aluminium discs) are seated in their slots and replace any chipped wafer from spares, put the handle back on with both tines in the notches and check it holds by lifting 1 cm by the bar. The tank stays dry.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; wafers fixed in the carrier (drawn, mass included); a tip past 15 deg is scored as wafers walking out of their slots. PFA flexure as sliders: legs and bow sprung at 2000 N/m; a code rule sets the legs' target 1.2 mm per mm of bow travel. Tines hold the carrier by contact (no weld). Bench: 40 kg free body. Masses estimated. No water: a filled bath would buoy the load about 3 N and damp the descent, so the drained tank is the harder case.
